analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is missing bounds validation in VarSizedBinSearchArrayOf::bsearch(): it uses header.unitSize/header.nUnits from untrusted font data to compute element addresses and calls p->cmp(key) without verifying that each probed record (at mid * unitSize) is fully within the sanitized object extent. In this PoV, a malformed kerx format-6 lookup table provides inconsistent binary-search header values so bsearch() returns/probes a pointer near the end of the buffer; cmp() then reads LookupSegmentSingle::first/last via BEInt, causing a 1-byte OOB read.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger path: hb-shape-fuzzer -> kerx processing -> KerxSubTableFormat6::get_kerning() -> LookupFormat2::get_value() -> VarSizedBinSearchArrayOf::bsearch(). A crafted AAT kerx subtable (format 6) with attacker-controlled lookup table header fields (notably unitSize/nUnits and layout near table end) must pass current sanitize checks yet allow bsearch probe addresses that are not safe for Type reads, so cmp() reads past allocation boundary.
